classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
items.description: Volumetric rate of coherent radio-frequency wave energy absorption by fast ions of a specified species and charge state or bundle, locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: Fast-ion charge-state power density is the rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves transfer energy directly to nonthermal fast ions of a specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle per unit physical volume. It encompasses local absorption and its flux-surface average, which represents deposition averaged over a magnetic flux surface. The local absorption density and its flux-surface-averaged form are defined by $$ p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}} = \sum_{z\in C}\frac{dP_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}}{dV}, \qquad p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} $$ where $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local fast-ion absorption density, $p_{\mathrm{f},C}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is its flux-surface average, $C$ is the selected set of ionic charge states, $z$ identifies an included charge state, $P_{\mathrm{f},z}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the wave power absorbed by fast ions in that state, $V$ is physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a flux-surface average. A single-state quantity includes only that charge state; a bundle is summed over its included states, not over every charge state of the species. The recipient population excludes thermal ions. The quantity describes direct wave absorption, not subsequent collisional redistribution, stored fast-ion energy, or volume-integrated absorbed power. This is the fast-population, direct-wave-absorption contribution to [ion charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), rather than its full net energy-source term. Summing nonoverlapping contributions over all ionic charge states gives [fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density) for the same species, wave content, and spatial averaging. The [toroidal-mode-resolved counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) additionally separates this absorption by toroidal Fourier mode.

items.name: forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Relative phase of the forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module, referenced to the first module for inter-module toroidal phasing.
items.documentation: The forward-wave phase is the relative phase angle of the complex radio-frequency power-wave phasor associated with one ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module. It describes inter-module phasing rather than an absolute phase. For selected module $i$, the relative forward-wave phase is defined by $$ \theta_i^{+} = \arg\left(\tilde{a}_i^{+}\right) - \arg\left(\tilde{a}_1^{+}\right) $$ where $\theta_i^{+}$ is the relative forward-wave phase, $i$ identifies the selected antenna module, module $1$ is the first reference module, $\tilde{a}_i^{+}$ is the complex phasor of the forward radio-frequency power wave associated with module $i$, and $\arg$ returns a phasor's phase angle. The quantity applies only to the forward wave at an antenna module and is defined relative to the first module; no absolute phase relative to a generator or external reference is implied. It concerns the electromagnetic power-wave phasor, not a plasma-particle quantity or a spatially distributed plasma field. This is the forward-wave specialization of the relative antenna phasor phase defined by [wave phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna). It is distinct from the relative phase of the reflected wave, [reflected phase of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna](name:reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and from the phase of the RF current carried by an antenna strap, [wave phase of an antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap). Sign convention: Positive when the selected module's forward-wave phasor leads the first reference module in phase.

items.name: straight_field_line_angle
items.description: An angular coordinate that labels position along magnetic field lines after a straight-field-line transformation, making field-line trajectories linear on each magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: A straight-field-line angle is an angular coordinate for labeling position along magnetic field lines in a magnetic-flux coordinate description. The transformation is chosen so that field-line trajectories are straight, or have constant angular slope, on each flux surface. This quantity denotes the coordinate itself rather than a mechanical steering angle, wave phase, or physical distance along a field line. Its origin, angular orientation, and selected angular direction are defined by the associated straight-field-line coordinate convention. The [poloidal straight-field-line angle](name:poloidal_straight_field_line_angle) is the poloidal specialization of this general coordinate concept. Other specializations, when defined, differ by the angular direction or coordinate convention rather than by a different underlying physical quantity. Sign convention: Positive when position advances in the defined positive direction of the straight-field-line angular coordinate.

items.name: total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
items.description: Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources through resonant electron-cyclotron interactions. It excludes launched, transmitted, reflected, and unabsorbed shine-through power.
items.documentation: Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources through resonant interaction with electrons at the electron cyclotron frequency or its harmonics. It is an absorbed heating power, not the generated, launched, transmitted, reflected, or unabsorbed radiofrequency power. The total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power is the sum of the net absorbed powers from the contributing electron-cyclotron sources: $$ P_\mathrm{EC} = \sum_{s=1}^{N_\mathrm{EC}} P_{\mathrm{EC},s} $$ where $N_\mathrm{EC}$ is the number of contributing electron-cyclotron sources, $P_{\mathrm{EC},s}$ is the net electron-cyclotron power absorbed by the plasma from source $s$ expressed in watts, and $P_\mathrm{EC}$ is the total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power expressed in watts. The per-source contribution is [power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating](name:power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating). This quantity is non-negative and is zero when no electron-cyclotron power is absorbed by the plasma; it is a component of [total_external_heating_power](name:total_external_heating_power) when total external heating is formed over all auxiliary heating methods.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
items.description: Vertical Z-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation: Vertical $Z$-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row is the projection of that row reference point onto $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. For a row reference point with position vector $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}}$, the coordinate is defined by: $$ Z_{\mathrm{row}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}} \cdot \hat{Z} $$ where $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This is a row-level coordinate and is distinct from the antenna-level [vertical coordinate of the lower-hybrid antenna](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). It is distinct from the row vertical extent. Sign convention: Positive when the row reference point lies in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame from the $Z=0$ plane.

items.name: current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive
items.description: Vector electric-current-density contribution generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive associated with plasma pressure and density gradients.
items.documentation: Current density due to bootstrap current drive is the vector contribution to electric current density generated by neoclassical bootstrap drive associated with plasma pressure and density gradients. It represents conventional electric-current flow produced by this drive mechanism, before selecting any particular component or projection. The quantity is scoped to the bootstrap-driven contribution only. It excludes current-density contributions from externally driven current, inductive electric fields, neutral beams, radio-frequency waves, or any total current density that aggregates multiple drive mechanisms. This parent quantity denotes the full vector bootstrap-current-density contribution. Component or projection quantities are more specific descendants; for example, [parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_bootstrap_current_drive) is the field-aligned projection of this vector along the magnetic-field direction, not a synonym for the full vector. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component represents conventional current flowing in the positive direction of that component or projection.

items.name: current_due_to_fusion_reactions
items.description: Net parallel plasma current generated by fusion reactions, associated with fast alpha particles produced by deuterium–tritium reactions and distinct from other non-inductive current-drive mechanisms.
items.documentation: This quantity is the net plasma current attributable to fusion reactions within the plasma, associated with fast alpha particles produced by deuterium–tritium reactions. It represents the parallel current contribution rather than the total plasma current. The defining relation is $$ I_{\mathrm{fus}} = \int_S \mathbf{j}_{\alpha} \cdot \mathbf{b}\, dS $$ where $I_{\mathrm{fus}}$ is the fusion-reaction-driven current, $\mathbf{j}_{\alpha}$ is the current-density vector carried by the fusion-born fast-alpha population, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector in the local magnetic-field direction, and $S$ is the cross-sectional surface through which the parallel current is evaluated; $dS$ is an element of that surface. The quantity is a net signed aggregation over the fusion-born alpha population and the relevant plasma cross section. It includes only the current attributable to fusion reactions and is not a local current density, a current magnitude, or an all-population current. It excludes current contributions driven by other mechanisms and must not be interpreted as the total plasma current or the total non-inductive current. It is an additive contribution to the non-inductive current balance. Sign convention: Positive when the fusion-reaction-driven conventional current is parallel to the local magnetic-field direction.

items.name: oxygen_density_at_divertor_target
items.description: Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume for oxygen ions at the sheath entrance, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
items.documentation: Number density of the oxygen species at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the oxygen-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). The local oxygen-ion number density is defined by the differential particle count: $$ n_{\rm O} = \frac{dN_{\rm O}}{dV} $$ where $N_{\rm O}$ is the total number of oxygen ions in a small plasma volume $V$ centered at the sheath entrance on the plasma side of the divertor target. This quantity applies to the oxygen-ion population at the specified divertor target and sums the number densities of all positive oxygen ionization states, counting each ion once. Neutral oxygen atoms are excluded; therefore, it is distinct from [oxygen_density](name:oxygen_density), which includes neutral oxygen as well as charged oxygen states. The target-specific quantity has the same charge-state-summed convention as [neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target), while [oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary) represents the corresponding oxygen-ion density at the plasma boundary without this divertor-target locus.

items.description: Number density of ions of a specified species at the plasma boundary, flux-surface averaged with inverse poloidal-flux-gradient weighting, summed over all charge states, and excluding neutral atoms and molecules.
items.documentation:
Number density of ion The flux-surface average is defined by $$ \langle n_iangle = \oint n_i\,dS/|
abla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|

abla\psi|$. This quantity is evaluated on the confined-plasma side of the plasma boundary. It is summed over all charge states of the represented ion species and excludes neutral atoms and molecules; distinct ion species are not implicitly combined. It is a flux-surface average, not a local point value, volume average, or chord average. The average is formed from the local [ion density at the plasma boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) by applying inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting over the surface. It differs from the [flux-surface-averaged total ion density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), which additionally aggregates charged-ion densities across ion species. The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Number density of xenon ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all xenon ion charge states and excluding neutral xenon.
items.documentation:
Number density of xenon The flux-surface average is defined by $$ \langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}angle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Xe}}\,dS/|
abla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|
abla\psi| $$ where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Xe}}angle$ is the averaged xenon-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the local xenon-ion number density, $S$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|
abla\psi|$. This quantity is charge-state-summed over xenon ions and is not a local point value, a volume average, or a density that includes neutral xenon. It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [xenon ion density at the plasma boundary](name:xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary), with inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting replacing the pointwise value by its surface mean. It differs from the [volume-averaged xenon density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which averages over the plasma volume rather than over the plasma-boundary surface. The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface. Related quantities: [flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary), [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for the tritium-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region. The local tritium-ion number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the tritium-ion distribution function at a boundary point: $$ n_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_\mathrm{T}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v $$ where $n_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is tritium-ion velocity, $f_\mathrm{T}$ is the tritium-ion phase-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity applies specifically to ionized tritium and excludes neutral tritium, deuterium, protium, electrons, impurity ions, and total ion density. It is a local boundary value, with no averaging over the boundary surface or over a volume; for tritium, the relevant positive ion population is singly ionized tritium, so no aggregation over multiple positive ionization stages is applied. It is the tritium-specific instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related flux-surface-averaged tritium density at the plasma boundary instead represents the average of tritium-ion density over the same last closed magnetic flux surface, while [hydrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [deuterium density at the plasma boundary](name:deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) refer to different hydrogen-isotope ion populations.

items.name: tungsten_density_at_separatrix
items.description: Tungsten-ion number density on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all positive ionization states and distinguished from its flux-surface average.
items.documentation: Tungsten-ion number density at the plasma boundary represents the local population of positively charged tungsten ions on the separatrix, the last closed magnetic flux surface. The same physical quantity may also be evaluated as a flux-surface average over that boundary surface; the local and averaged forms are distinct. The charge-state-summed local density is defined from the velocity distributions by: $$ n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{Z=1}^{Z_{\max}} \int f_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the tungsten-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is a position on the separatrix, $Z$ is the positive tungsten ion charge state, $Z_{\max}$ is the highest included charge state, $f_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z}$ is the velocity distribution of that charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity applies to tungsten ions evaluated at the plasma boundary and sums over all positive ionization states. It excludes neutral tungsten and does not select an individual charge state. The local form is evaluated at a boundary position, whereas the flux-surface-averaged tungsten density at the plasma boundary averages the same charge-state-summed density over the boundary flux surface. The flux-surface-averaged quantity is therefore an aggregation of this local density over the same separatrix, not a different species or charge-state convention. It is distinct from [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), which averages tungsten-ion density over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

items.name: radiative_temperature_at_ece_channel

items.documentation:
Radiative temperature at an ECE channel is the equivalent blackbody temperature associated with the detected electron cyclotron emission intensity at that channel's selected frequency. It is a brightness-temperature representation of the radiation, not the kinetic temperature of the electron population. For specific intensity represented by a blackbody spectrum, the radiation temperature $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is defined by $$ I_
