u$ is the detected specific intensity at frequency $
u$, $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light, and $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the energy-equivalent blackbody temperature. The quantity applies to one ECE channel and its selected frequency; it is not summed or averaged over channels. It excludes the separate kinetic electron temperature and polarization-resolved radiation quantities. When the emitting plasma is optically thick, $T_{\mathrm{rad}}$ approaches the local electron temperature. The [radiative temperature at the magnetic axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis) uses the same brightness-temperature definition at a different evaluation locus.

items.name: refractive_index
items.description: Dimensionless ratio of an electromagnetic wave’s phase-gradient vector to its vacuum wavenumber, retaining propagation direction and signed components.
items.documentation: The refractive-index vector describes electromagnetic phase propagation relative to propagation in vacuum. It preserves the direction of the wave phase gradient while expressing its magnitude relative to the vacuum reference. The defining relation is $$ \mathbf{n} = \frac{\mathbf{k}}{k_0}, \qquad k_0 = \frac{\omega}{c} $$ where $\mathbf{n}$ is the refractive-index vector, $\mathbf{k}$ is the wave vector, $k_0$ is the vacuum wavenumber, $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency, and $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum. Directional representations include the projection parallel to the local magnetic field, represented by [parallel_refractive_index](name:parallel_refractive_index), and the magnitude of the perpendicular projection, represented by [perpendicular_refractive_index](name:perpendicular_refractive_index). The same normalized phase-propagation concept applies to propagation through an optical element.

items.name: current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux
items.description: Current-weighted average external magnetic flux is the component-wise mean of magnetic flux produced by sources outside the plasma, weighted over the plasma current-carrying region by the corresponding current density. It excludes flux generated by the plasma current itself; concrete children specify components such as the poloidal component.
items.documentation: Current-weighted average external magnetic flux is the component-wise mean of externally generated magnetic flux over the plasma current-carrying region. It represents the part of the magnetic flux linked by the plasma current that is generated by sources outside the plasma, with the plasma self-generated flux excluded. For any component $a$, the current-weighted component average is $$ \overline{\Phi}_{\mathrm{ext},a}^{J} = \frac{\int_{\Omega_a} \Phi_{\mathrm{ext},a}(\mathbf{x})\, j_a(\mathbf{x})\, dA} {\int_{\Omega_a} j_a(\mathbf{x})\, dA} $$ where $a$ labels a magnetic-flux component, $\overline{\Phi}_{\mathrm{ext},a}^{J}$ is the current-weighted average external magnetic-flux component, $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext},a}(\mathbf{x})$ is the externally generated magnetic-flux component at position $\mathbf{x}$, $j_a(\mathbf{x})$ is the corresponding plasma current-density component used as the weight, $\Omega_a$ is the current-carrying plasma cross-section for that component, and $dA$ is its area element. The denominator is the corresponding total plasma current component and must be nonzero. This parent quantity does not specify a particular magnetic-flux component or surface orientation. Concrete component names supply that specialization; for example, [poloidal current-weighted average external magnetic flux](name:poloidal_current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux) is the poloidal component. External magnetic flux includes contributions from active conductors and passive induced currents outside the plasma and excludes flux produced by the plasma current. Sign convention: Positive when the current-density-weighted integral of the selected external magnetic-flux component has the same sign as the total plasma current component used for its normalization, with both signs evaluated in the positive orientation of that component.

items.name: poloidal_beta
items.description: Poloidal beta compares volume-averaged total perpendicular plasma pressure with a magnetic-pressure scale set by the net plasma current and reference major radius.
items.documentation: Poloidal beta is the ratio of volume-averaged total perpendicular plasma pressure to a reference poloidal magnetic-pressure scale. The reference scale is defined by a whole-plasma, current-based normalization rather than by the poloidal field at a particular point. The defining pressure ratio and its current-based normalization are $$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$ Here $\beta_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal beta, $p$ is total perpendicular plasma pressure, $V$ is the entire plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\langle p\rangle$ is the pressure averaged over that volume. The quantities $R_0$, $I_{\mathrm{p}}$, and $\mu_0$ are the reference major radius, net toroidal plasma current, and vacuum permeability, respectively. The effective reference poloidal field $B_{\mathrm{p,ref}}$ satisfies $B_{\mathrm{p,ref}}^2=\mu_0^2 I_{\mathrm{p}}^2R_0/(2V)$; it is not a local poloidal-field magnitude. The pressure includes contributions from all plasma populations, rather than electrons alone or only thermal particles. This global quantity differs from a point-local or pedestal-top electron beta. The definition requires nonzero net plasma current and a positive reference major radius. Poloidal beta is the poloidal-field-normalized member of the [beta](name:beta) family, whereas [toroidal beta](name:toroidal_beta) uses a reference toroidal magnetic field. For the same pressure average and a combined reference field formed by adding the squared poloidal and toroidal reference fields, $1/\beta=1/\beta_{\mathrm{p}}+1/\beta_{\mathrm{t}}$, where $\beta$ is combined-field beta and $\beta_{\mathrm{t}}$ is toroidal beta.

items.name: total_counter_passing_particle_pressure
items.description: Total pressure of counter-passing particles is the flux-surface average of one-third of their kinetic-stress trace, including thermal, nonthermal, and directed-motion contributions.
items.documentation: Total pressure of counter-passing particles is the flux-surface-averaged isotropic part of the kinetic stress carried by the thermal and nonthermal populations of a specified species. Counter-passing particles occupy untrapped guiding-center orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current. The nonrelativistic kinetic definition is $$ p_{s,\mathrm{cp}} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{3}\int_{\mathrm{cp}} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} $$ where $p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}$ is the total counter-passing pressure of species $s$, $m_s$ is its particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the [particle distribution](name:particle_distribution) including its thermal and nonthermal parts, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integration domain $\mathrm{cp}$ selects counter-passing orbits, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a magnetic-flux-surface average weighted by the differential volume between neighboring surfaces. Velocity is not centered on the counter-passing population's mean flow, so directed-motion stress is retained. “Total” denotes the additive thermal and nonthermal contributions within the specified species, not a sum over all plasma species. Contributions from multiple distributions representing that species are superposed. Trapped and co-passing particles are excluded. This quantity is a flux-surface average rather than a local pressure at a point on the surface; it combines all three velocity degrees of freedom without assuming isotropy and is not a single field-parallel or field-perpendicular stress component. The [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) restricts the kinetic moment to suprathermal particles, whereas this quantity also includes the thermal contribution. The [total co-passing particle pressure](name:total_co_passing_particle_pressure) applies the thermal-plus-nonthermal scope to the opposite passing-orbit class.

items.name: accumulated_deuterated_methane_prefill_count
items.description: Cumulative pre-breakdown inventory of deuterated methane (CD4), weighted by ten equivalent electrons per molecule rather than reported as a molecular count.
items.documentation: This quantity is the cumulative amount of deuterated methane introduced during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory. It represents neutral CD4 molecules before plasma breakdown, not the post-breakdown gas-injection inventory. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm prefill} = \int_{t_0}^{t_b} \dot{N}_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm CD_4}(t)\,dt = 10N_{\rm CD_4}^{\rm prefill} $$ where $N_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm prefill}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron inventory, $\dot{N}_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm CD_4}$ is the [deuterated methane source rate](name:deuterated_methane_source_rate), $t_0$ and $t_b$ delimit prefill before breakdown, and $N_{\rm CD_4}^{\rm prefill}$ is the accumulated number of CD4 molecules. The factor ten is the total electron count of one fully ionizable CD4 molecule. The species-resolved quantity contributes to the [accumulated total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count), which sums equivalent-electron inventories across gas species.

items.name: ipb98y2_confinement_time
items.description: IPB98(y,2) empirical-scaling reference for global energy confinement time, providing the denominator for the H98 confinement enhancement factor.
items.documentation: The IPB98(y,2) energy confinement time is the global energy-confinement timescale predicted by the IPB98(y,2) empirical scaling law. It is an energy-channel performance benchmark rather than a species-resolved or local transport time. The underlying global energy confinement time is defined by $$ \tau_E = \frac{W}{P_{\mathrm{loss}}} $$ where $\tau_E$ is the global energy confinement time, $W$ is the total thermal energy stored in the plasma, and $P_{\mathrm{loss}}$ is the net power leaving the plasma. The quantity documented here is the IPB98(y,2) scaling prediction of this timescale, not the directly evaluated confinement time for a particular plasma state. The value applies to the complete plasma energy content and its global loss balance; it is not a local profile quantity, a particle confinement time, or a confinement time assigned to an individual species. It is a single empirical reference value for the energy channel. The [energy confinement enhancement factor](name:energy_confinement_enhancement_factor) compares the actual global energy confinement time with this reference through $H_{98} = \tau_E / \tau_{E,98}$, where $H_{98}$ is the dimensionless confinement enhancement factor and $\tau_{E,98}$ is this IPB98(y,2) scaling prediction.

items.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Radial component of a first-order perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region for a toroidal linear-MHD mode, represented by its real or imaginary coefficient.
items.documentation: The quantity is the radial projection of a first-order, complex perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region. It is the common radial coefficient represented by separate real and imaginary quadratures. $$ \widetilde{A}_{1R} = \widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_1 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}} $$ where $\widetilde{A}_{1R}$ is the complex radial vector-potential coefficient, $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_1$ is the complex first-order perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major-radius coordinate $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The subscript $1$ denotes the first-order perturbation. The quantity applies to the vacuum-region radial component associated with a toroidal linear-MHD mode. It represents one mode without summing over toroidal modes and includes both quadratures; it is not restricted to either the real or imaginary coefficient alone. It excludes the complete vector potential and its poloidal and toroidal components. The full vector quantity is [perturbed vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), of which this quantity is the radial projection. Its two quadrature-specific representations are the [real part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part) and [imaginary part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part) of the same complex radial coefficient. Sign convention: Positive when the radial vector-potential coefficient points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description: Time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the time-averaged amplitude of a magnetic-field perturbation projected along the local equilibrium magnetic field and normalized by a reference magnetic-field magnitude. It does not include flux-surface averaging unless a more specific name states that aggregation.
items.documentation: Time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the time-averaged scalar amplitude of the component of a magnetic-field perturbation parallel to the local equilibrium magnetic field, normalized by a reference magnetic-field magnitude. It characterizes the parallel perturbation amplitude after the sign of the parallel projection has been removed. The quantity is defined by averaging the normalized magnitude of the parallel perturbation over the time interval defining the quantity: $$ \overline{b}_{\parallel,\mathrm{pert}} = \left\langle \frac{\left|\delta \mathbf{B}\cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}_0\right|}{B_\mathrm{ref}} \right\rangle_t $$ where $\overline{b}_{\parallel,\mathrm{pert}}$ is the time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude, $\delta \mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field perturbation, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_0$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic field, $B_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference magnetic-field magnitude used for normalization, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes averaging over the time interval defining the quantity. The scope is the time-averaged scalar amplitude before any spatial aggregation is added by a more specific qualifier. It applies wherever the magnetic-field perturbation, local equilibrium-field direction, and normalization reference are defined; this parent by itself does not prescribe a flux-surface, volume, line, or ensemble average. This is not the instantaneous normalized perturbation, the signed normalized parallel component, the perpendicular perturbation, or the total magnetic-perturbation magnitude. The absolute value distinguishes it from signed parallel-field perturbations by discarding the sign of the parallel projection. The [flux-surface-averaged time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude) is obtained by applying an additional magnetic-flux-surface average to this already time-averaged quantity; the additional qualifier changes the spatial aggregation, not the presence of time averaging.

items.name: pulse_duration
items.description: Elapsed duration of the confined-plasma phase in a single discharge, from plasma breakdown until termination of the confined plasma.
items.documentation: Elapsed duration from plasma breakdown until termination of auxiliary heating in a single discharge.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil
items.description: Radial coordinate of a Rogowski coil position, equal to the major-radius coordinate of the coil's designated geometric point in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The radial coordinate of a Rogowski coil position is the major-radius coordinate of the designated geometric point representing the coil position. It is the non-negative perpendicular distance of that point from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Using any point on the toroidal symmetry axis as reference, the coordinate is defined by the transverse projection of the coil-position vector relative to that axis: $$ R_{\mathrm{coil}} = \left\| (\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{coil}} - \mathbf{o}_{\mathcal{A}}) - \left[(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{coil}} - \mathbf{o}_{\mathcal{A}}) \cdot \hat{Z}\right]\hat{Z} \right\| $$ where $R_{\mathrm{coil}}$ is the radial coordinate of the Rogowski coil position, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{coil}}$ is the position vector of the designated geometric point, $\mathbf{o}_{\mathcal{A}}$ is any position vector on the toroidal symmetry axis $\mathcal{A}$, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector along that axis, and $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm. This quantity applies to the single designated geometric point used to locate the Rogowski coil. It is not an average, integral, or other aggregation over the winding path, aperture, conductor cross-section, or physical extent of the coil. This coordinate is the radial member of the Rogowski-coil position coordinates and is distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the Rogowski coil](name:vertical_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil) and any toroidal angular coordinate of the same point. It is also distinct from the [area of the Rogowski coil](name:area_of_rogowski_coil), the [current of the Rogowski coil](name:current_of_rogowski_coil), coil orientation, and winding geometry; those quantities do not change the definition of $R_{\mathrm{coil}}$. As a named instance of [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), it is invariant under changes of toroidal angle at fixed major radius.

items.name: area_of_passive_loop
items.description: Area of a passive loop is the non-negative cross-sectional area of conducting material in a passive loop element, taken on a section normal to the local current path. It excludes the aperture enclosed by the loop.
items.documentation: Area of a passive loop is the non-negative cross-sectional area of the solid conducting material of a passive conducting loop element, evaluated on a surface normal to the local current path. It is a material cross-section of the conductor, not the aperture enclosed by the loop or the area swept out by the loop centerline. The general geometric definition is the area of the conducting region $\mathcal{S}$ in that normal cross-section: $$ A = \int_{\mathcal{S}} dS $$ where $A$ is the passive-loop conductor area, $\mathcal{S}$ is the subset of the section occupied by conducting material, and $dS$ is the scalar surface-area element. For an annular cross-section, this definition gives $A = \pi(r_o^2-r_i^2)$, where $r_i$ and $r_o$ are the [inner](name:inner_radius_of_passive_loop) and [outer](name:outer_radius_of_passive_loop) radii measured from the annulus center to the conducting boundaries. For a non-annular cross-section, $\mathcal{S}$ is the bounded conducting region defined by the conductor geometry; parameters such as thickness, width, or height describe that boundary but are not themselves the area.

items.name: vertical_force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Signed vertical component of the net electromagnetic Lorentz force on one poloidal-field coil, resolved along increasing Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: This quantity is the net electromagnetic Lorentz force on an individual poloidal-field-coil conductor projected onto the vertical axis of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The force component is defined by $$ F_Z = \int_{V_{\mathrm{coil}}} (\mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}\,\mathrm{d}V $$ where $F_Z$ is the vertical force component, $V_{\mathrm{coil}}$ is the conductor volume, $\mathbf{J}$ is the current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector acting on the conductor, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is a differential volume element. This is a signed component rather than the force magnitude or resultant. The radial component is represented separately by [radial force of a poloidal-field coil](name:radial_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), while [force of a poloidal-field coil](name:force_of_poloidal_field_coil) represents the coil’s electromagnetic force resultant. Sign convention: Positive when the net force points toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: width_of_correction_coil
items.description: Full non-negative extent of a non-axisymmetric correction-coil conductor cross-section measured along its local normal axis; for circular sections it is the diameter, and for annular sections it is the outer diameter.
items.documentation: Full non-negative extent of a non-axisymmetric correction-coil conductor cross-section measured along its local normal axis is the characteristic transverse size of that cross-section. It is a geometric property of the conductor cross-section, not a signed displacement or orientation. The defining geometric identification is: $$ w = \begin{cases} a_n, & \text{rectangular or square cross-section},\\ D, & \text{circular cross-section},\\ D_{\mathrm{out}}, & \text{annular cross-section}. \end{cases} $$ where $w$ is this width, $a_n$ is the full cross-section extent along the local normal axis, $D$ is the circular cross-section diameter, and $D_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the annular cross-section outer diameter. The scope is one conductor cross-section of one non-axisymmetric correction coil; the quantity is assigned to the whole cross-section. It is not a sum or average over multiple coils, separate conductor segments, or turns, and it is not the conductor path length or the spatial location of the coil. The companion linear size for a rectangular or square section is the [height of a correction-coil conductor cross-section](name:height_of_correction_coil); the [area of a correction-coil conductor cross-section](name:area_of_correction_coil) is the corresponding area, not another linear dimension. For an annular section, the [inner radius of a correction-coil conductor cross-section](name:inner_radius_of_correction_coil) describes the central opening, whereas this width describes the outer diameter. The [width of a toroidal-field-coil conductor cross-section](name:width_of_toroidal_field_coil) is the analogous geometric quantity for a toroidal-field coil rather than a non-axisymmetric correction coil.

items.name: plasma_temperature
items.description: Effective temperature of the plasma in a fluid or MHD description, representing the average thermal kinetic energy per degree of freedom of the combined charged particle population.
items.documentation: The plasma temperature is a fundamental thermodynamic state variable in fluid and single-fluid MHD models, quantifying the mean random kinetic energy of the charged particle population. In a single-fluid description it is linked to thermal pressure via the equation of state $$ p = n k_B T $$ where $p$ is the scalar pressure, $n$ is the total particle number density, and $k_B$ is the Boltzmann constant. In multi-species plasmas an effective plasma temperature may be obtained as a density-weighted combination of electron and ion contributions; applications requiring species resolution use explicitly qualified forms such as particle_temperature or [neutral_temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature). This quantity also appears as the equilibrium background in linear MHD stability analysis, where its first-order perturbation is represented by the complex eigenfunction perturbed_plasma_temperature, encoding the amplitude and phase of the temperature fluctuation for a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic. The total isotropic pressure of the plasma, including contributions summed over all species, is captured by plasma_pressure.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary
items.description: Poloidal magnetic flux evaluated on the outermost flux surface of the halo-current region during a disruption. This is the wall-side halo boundary of the halo-current domain, not the inner confined-plasma interface.
items.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux at the halo boundary is the value of the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function on the outermost magnetic flux surface of the halo-current region during a disruption. The halo boundary is the wall-side flux-surface limit of the halo-current domain, not the inner interface between that domain and any confined-plasma core. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical height, the value on a halo-boundary point $(R_h, Z_h)$ is defined by the flux of the vertical magnetic field through the horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis: $$ \psi_h = \psi(R_h, Z_h) = \int_0^{R_h} B_Z(R', Z_h)\,2\pi R'\,dR' $$ where $\psi_h$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at the halo boundary, $\psi(R_h, Z_h)$ is the poloidal magnetic flux function evaluated on that boundary, and $B_Z$ is the vertical component of the magnetic field. This quantity is the poloidal-flux counterpart of the [toroidal magnetic flux at the halo boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary). It is a flux-surface value and does not denote the total magnetic flux through the halo-current volume or the halo current itself. Sign convention: Positive when $B_Z$ on the integration disk points in the $+Z$ direction.

items.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density
items.description: Mean relativistic kinetic energy per unit volume of the runaway electron population, obtained by averaging the local kinetic energy density over the confined plasma volume.
items.documentation: The volume-averaged runaway electron kinetic energy density is a global scalar characterizing the mean suprathermal energy stored per unit volume in the runaway electron (RE) population. It is obtained by integrating the local relativistic kinetic energy density over the total confined plasma volume $V$ and dividing by $V$. The underlying local quantity is the relativistic kinetic energy moment of the RE distribution function: $$ u_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r}) = \int f_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{p})\,(\gamma - 1)\,m_e c^2 \, d^3p $$ where $f_\mathrm{RE}$ is the runaway electron phase-space distribution function, $\gamma = (1 + p^2 / m_e^2 c^2)^{1/2}$ is the Lorentz factor, $m_e$ is the electron rest mass, $c$ is the speed of light, and $\mathbf{p}$ is the relativistic momentum. The volume average is then $\langle u_\mathrm{RE} \rangle = V^{-1} \int_V u_\mathrm{RE}\,dV$. This quantity is evaluated from kinetic or reduced-fluid runaway electron models, particularly in disruption current-quench simulations where RE populations can reach energies of several to tens of MeV per particle. Multiplying by the plasma volume $V$ recovers the total stored relativistic energy given by [runaway_electron_kinetic_energy](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy). The local non-averaged counterpart is runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density, and the corresponding global particle number density is [volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density).

items.name: x_first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge
items.description: Signed direction cosine of a sensor’s unit measurement-direction vector along the x axis of the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation: This quantity is the x-directed component of a sensor’s oriented measurement-direction vector. It describes orientation rather than the sensor’s spatial attachment location, which is specified separately by the [x coordinate of the sensor attachment point](name:x_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point). The direction cosine is defined by $$ d_x = \hat{\mathbf d} \cdot \hat{\mathbf x} $$ where $\hat{\mathbf d}$ is the sensor’s unit measurement-direction vector and $\hat{\mathbf x}$ is the unit vector along the x axis of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. For a normalized direction vector, $-1 \leq d_x \leq 1$; the corresponding y- and z-axis components are represented by the [y direction unit vector of the sensor](name:y_first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge) and [z direction unit vector of the sensor](name:z_first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge). Sign convention: Positive when the sensor’s measurement direction has a component toward increasing x.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_neutron_detector
items.description: Full transverse extent of the rectangular collimating aperture associated with a neutron detector, measured between its edges along the aperture’s first local tangential direction.
items.documentation: This quantity is the full transverse width of the neutron detector’s collimating aperture along its first local tangential direction. It describes the aperture opening rather than the external detector body, housing, or shielding. The width is defined by $$ w_1 = x_{1,\max} - x_{1,\min} $$ where $w_1$ is the first local tangential aperture width, and $x_{1,\max}$ and $x_{1,\min}$ are the positions of the two aperture edges along the first local tangential axis. This quantity applies only to a rectangular aperture and represents the complete edge-to-edge opening dimension, not a radius or half-width. The other transverse dimension is represented by the second local tangential width of the neutron detector, whereas a circular opening is characterized by the [radius of the neutron detector](name:radius_of_neutron_detector) rather than by rectangular widths.

items.name: total_neutron_rate
items.description: Total neutron emission rate produced by deuterium–tritium, deuterium–deuterium, and tritium–tritium fusion reactions in the plasma.
items.documentation: This quantity is the aggregate number of neutrons emitted per unit time by fusion reactions in the plasma. The total rate is the sum of the neutron-emission rates from the included fusion channels: $$ S_n = R_{n,\mathrm{DT}} + R_{n,\mathrm{DD}} + R_{n,\mathrm{TT}} $$ where $S_n$ is the total neutron emission rate, and $R_{n,\mathrm{DT}}$, $R_{n,\mathrm{DD}}$, and $R_{n,\mathrm{TT}}$ are the neutron-emission rates from deuterium–tritium, deuterium–deuterium, and tritium–tritium fusion reactions, respectively. The quantity includes all three stated fusion reaction channels and their combined neutron production; it is not restricted to a single reaction channel, neutron energy group, or local spatial region. It represents an aggregate emission rate rather than a neutron flux per unit area. The [deuterium–tritium neutron flux](name:deuterium_tritium_flux) describes the deuterium–tritium channel contribution, which is included in this total together with the deuterium–deuterium and tritium–tritium contributions.

items.name: line_averaged_boron_density
items.description: Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all boron ionization states, giving a chord-averaged measure of elemental boron impurity content.
items.documentation: Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all ionization states of boron, so it represents the chord-averaged elemental boron impurity content rather than a local point value. The line average over a chord of path length $L$ is defined by the path integral of the local charge-state-summed boron density along arc length $l$: $$ \bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{z=0}^{5} n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)\, dl $$ where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell}$ is the line-averaged boron density, $n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)$ is the local boron number density in ionization state $z$ at position $l$ along the chord, $z=0$ denotes neutral boron, $z=5$ denotes fully stripped B$^{5+}$, and $L$ is the total path length used for the average. This quantity is a chord average of the charge-state-summed elemental [boron density](name:boron_density); it is not a charge-state-resolved boron density and does not exclude neutral boron. It differs from [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density), which averages the same elemental density over the confined plasma volume.

items.name: accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms introduced by gas injection during plasma prefill before plasma breakdown, with two count units assigned per atom.
items.documentation: The quantity is the cumulative inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It covers injection before plasma breakdown and excludes helium-3 introduced after breakdown. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} = 2\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t)\,dt $$ where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number, $N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injected helium-3 atom count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injection rate in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in s. This is the pre-breakdown counterpart of [accumulated helium-3 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection); [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) represents the instantaneous rate rather than the accumulated inventory.

items.name: accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
items.description: Cumulative number of particles released by ablation from an injected pellet up to a specified position along its trajectory.
items.documentation: This quantity is the cumulative particle release from pellet ablation as the pellet travels through the plasma. It counts particles removed from the pellet up to the specified trajectory position, rather than particles remaining in the pellet. The accumulated release at path distance $\ell$ is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{abl}}(\ell)=\int_{\ell_0}^{\ell}\frac{dN_{\mathrm{abl}}}{d\ell'}\,d\ell' $$ where $N_{\mathrm{abl}}$ is the dimensionless released-particle count, $\ell$ and $\ell'$ are distances along the pellet trajectory in m, $\ell_0$ is the trajectory entry position, and $dN_{\mathrm{abl}}/d\ell'$ is the local ablation release per unit path distance. The count is nondecreasing along the trajectory when the ablation release rate is nonnegative. It represents deposited pellet material and is distinct from the initial pellet inventory given by count of pellet.

items.name: boron_density_at_limiter
items.description: Boron ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral boron atoms.
items.documentation: Boron density at a limiter is the local number density of boron ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. $$ n_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}=\sum_{q=1}^{5}n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L) $$ where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of counted boron ions, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, $n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the density of boron charge state $q$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The sum includes boron ions from B$^{+}$ through fully stripped B$^{5+}$ and excludes neutral boron atoms. This is the boron-specific specialization of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter); unlike [boron density at the plasma boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary), it is evaluated specifically at the limiter-side location.

items.name: surface_emissivity
items.description: Dimensionless ratio of thermal radiation emitted by a surface to blackbody radiation at the same surface temperature, with the stated spectral and angular averaging.
items.documentation: Surface emissivity is the effectiveness of a material surface in emitting thermal electromagnetic radiation relative to an ideal blackbody at the same temperature. It is a material property of the emitting surface and is distinct from the emitted energy flux described by [energy flux due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). The effective emissivity is defined by $$ \varepsilon = \frac{M_{\mathrm{emit}}(T_s)}{M_{\mathrm{bb}}(T_s)} $$ where $M_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the surface thermal radiative exitance, $M_{\mathrm{bb}}$ is the blackbody exitance, and $T_s$ is the surface temperature. The ratio applies to the specified spectral band and angular averaging; it is not a wavelength- and direction-resolved emissivity. Incident radiation and geometric surface area, such as optical-element area, are excluded.

items.name: y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera
items.description: Y-axis component of a camera’s image-up orientation unit vector, expressed in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation: The camera image-up unit vector specifies the orientation of increasing image-up direction, distinct from the camera line-of-sight direction. This quantity is its projection onto the Cartesian y-axis. $$ u_{\mathrm{up},y} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{up}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}} $$ where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{up}}$ is the image-up orientation unit vector and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y-axis unit vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The complete image-up vector has unit magnitude, so its components satisfy $u_{\mathrm{up},x}^2 + u_{\mathrm{up},y}^2 + u_{\mathrm{up},z}^2 = 1$. This component is distinct from the camera line-of-sight components represented by [x-direction unit vector of camera](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [z-direction unit vector of camera](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera).

items.name: extent_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description: Full end-to-end physical size of a soft X-ray detector along the applicable horizontal or vertical detector-plane direction.
items.documentation: The detector extent is the complete end-to-end linear size of the soft X-ray detector along one specified detector-plane direction. It characterizes the physical detector boundary rather than a spectral or radiometric property. For a coordinate $s$ measured along the selected detector-plane direction, the extent $L$ is defined by $$ L = s_{\max} - s_{\min} $$ where $s_{\max}$ and $s_{\min}$ are the coordinates of the two opposite physical boundaries. The applicable direction is horizontal or vertical within the detector plane. This quantity describes an overall detector dimension and is distinct from pixel dimensions, collecting [area of a diagnostic aperture](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture), and optical throughput such as the [étendue of a hard X-ray detector](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector).

items.name: spectral_wavelength_of_optical_element
items.description: Wavelength at an optical element specifies the vacuum spectral position at which its transmission, absorption, or other wavelength-dependent optical properties are evaluated.
items.documentation: Wavelength of optical element The defining relation is $$ \lambda = \frac{c}{\nu} $$ where $\lambda$ is the vacuum wavelength, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, and $\nu$ is the radiation frequency. Each value denotes a spectral evaluation point, not a response amplitude or wavelength interval. It does not inherently designate a passband center or edge, and it denotes the vacuum wavelength rather than the wavelength within the element's material. The definition is not restricted to a particular spectral band. The [spectral refractive index of an optical element](name:spectral_refractive_index_of_optical_element) and, for a filter, the [spectral absorptivity](name:spectral_absorptivity_of_filter) are response quantities evaluated as functions of this wavelength.

items.name: volume_averaged_total_runaway_electron_source_rate
items.description: Plasma-volume-averaged volumetric production rate of runaway electrons, summed over Dreicer, avalanche, hot-tail, Compton, and tritium-decay generation mechanisms.
items.documentation: Plasma-volume-averaged volumetric production rate of runaway electrons is the spatial average, over the plasma volume, of the local total rate at which electrons enter the runaway population. The total rate includes generation by Dreicer, avalanche, hot-tail, Compton, and tritium-decay mechanisms. The volume average is defined by $$ \left\langle S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}\right\rangle_V = \frac{1}{|\Omega_p|}\int_{\Omega_p} S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $\left\langle S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}\right\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged total runaway electron source rate, $S_{\mathrm{RE,total}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the total runaway electron source rate at position $\mathbf{x}$, $\Omega_p$ is the plasma-volume domain, $|\Omega_p|$ is the volume measure of that domain, and $dV$ is the volume element. This quantity applies to the runaway-electron population within the plasma volume and uses an unweighted volume average of the total local volumetric production rate. The mechanism sum is part of the quantity definition; the total includes component production rates such as the [Dreicer runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer) and the [hot-tail runaway electron source rate](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail), but is not restricted to either component. It is the plasma-volume-averaged counterpart of the total runaway electron source rate. It is a production-rate density averaged over volume, not the absolute number of runaway electrons and not a current-density measure; in particular it is distinct from the [volume-averaged parallel runaway electron current density](name:volume_averaged_parallel_runaway_electron_current_density), which describes charge transport by the runaway population.

items.name: surface_area_of_detector
items.description: Geometric surface area of the detector face defining the physical extent of one diagnostic detector.
items.documentation: This quantity is the geometric area of the specified detector surface associated with one diagnostic channel. It characterizes the physical extent of that detector surface as defined by its boundary and geometry. The surface area is defined by $$ A_{\mathrm{det}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{det}}} dA $$ where $A_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the detector surface area, $S_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the specified detector surface, and $dA$ is the differential surface-area element. The quantity applies to one detector and is not an aggregate over multiple channels or diagnostic components. It describes geometric surface extent, not a radiation or particle flux, detector response, or sensitivity. The detector surface is distinct from the designated diagnostic aperture described by [area of diagnostic aperture](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture), even when the two geometric surfaces coincide. It follows the same surface-area concept as [surface area of neutron detector](name:surface_area_of_neutron_detector), but is associated with the specified detector rather than specifically with a neutron-sensitive detector.

items.name: beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Particle number density of the beryllium ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local beryllium-ion count per physical volume there, summed over all beryllium ionization states.
items.documentation: Particle number density of the beryllium ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local beryllium-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all beryllium ionization states. It represents beryllium ions specifically, rather than neutral beryllium, electrons, or other ion species. The defining relation is $$ n_{\mathrm{Be},\mathrm{axis}} = \sum_Z n_{\mathrm{Be}^{Z+},\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Be}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Be},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the total beryllium-ion number density at the magnetic axis, $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{Z+},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in charge state $Z$, $Z$ is the ionic charge-state number, $N_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the number of beryllium ions included in the sum, and $V$ is physical volume. The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete beryllium-ion population at that location and is summed over all beryllium ionic charge states. It excludes neutral beryllium and is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor the density of another species. This is the beryllium-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). Like [boron density at the magnetic axis](name:boron_density_at_magnetic_axis), it is species-resolved while retaining charge-state aggregation; it differs from [beryllium density at the plasma boundary](name:beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary) only in its evaluation locus.

items.name: bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
items.description: Bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state, given by the first moment of their velocity distribution.
items.documentation: The quantity is the bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles occupying one specified internal state, such as a quantum or energy state. It retains resolution of that state rather than combining distinct neutral internal states. The state-resolved bulk velocity is the first velocity moment of the corresponding distribution: $$ \mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}} = \frac{\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}{\int f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}} $$ where $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$ is the state-resolved bulk neutral velocity, $\alpha$ identifies the internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{\alpha}$ is the neutral-particle velocity distribution for that state. This is the direction-agnostic vector parent for component projections of the same bulk neutral population in the same resolved internal state; it is not itself a radial, toroidal, poloidal, or vertical component. Component quantities such as [vertical bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity) are projections of this vector, with the vertical component defined along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes thermal speed and velocity spread, which are moments about the bulk velocity rather than this first velocity moment. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved cylindrical component is directed along the corresponding positive unit vector $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, restricted to co-passing orbit-class contributions and without restricting spatial direction.
items.documentation: Co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal ion population by Coulomb collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is restricted to the co-passing orbit-class contribution of those collisions and is represented by the full torque-density vector, not by a single spatial component. For the selected thermal-ion population, the co-passing collisional torque-density vector is defined from the co-passing contribution to its collision operator by $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v}) $$ where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the thermal-ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the thermal-ion distribution function, and $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the Coulomb-collision operator term giving momentum transfer to thermal ions from the co-passing orbit-class contribution. Co-passing denotes passing-orbit contributions whose toroidal motion in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is in the same sense as the plasma current, distinct from counter-passing and trapped orbit-class contributions. At parent level, the quantity retains the full vector direction for that orbit class; [toroidal co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding $\hat{\phi}$-component restriction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes torque deposited in fast-ion populations. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque-density component points along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Volumetric counter-passing torque density deposited in the fast-electron population through Coulomb collisions, the local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
items.documentation: The counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque density is the net rate at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum per unit volume to the counter-passing suprathermal electron population. It is the orbit-class specialization of [fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The vector torque density is defined from the corresponding collisional force density by $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}=\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{f}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}} $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin, and $\mathbf{f}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to counter-passing fast electrons. Its toroidal projection is [toroidal counter-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The quantity excludes thermal-electron and other orbit-class contributions. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Local particle concentration of a specified plasma population at the magnetic axis, with ion charge states aggregated and compound fuel mixtures treated as defined populations.
items.documentation: Particle number density at the magnetic axis is the local number of particles of a specified plasma population per physical volume at the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. The quantity is population-specific and does not denote an unrestricted sum over all plasma species. It is defined locally by: $$ n_P(\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis}) = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{N_P(\Delta V;\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis})}{\Delta V} $$ where $n_P$ is the particle number density of population $P$, $\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis}$ is the location of the magnetic axis, $N_P(\Delta V;\mathbf{x}_{\rm axis})$ is the number of particles from population $P$ within a physical volume $\Delta V$ centered at that location, and $\Delta V$ is the shrinking volume used to define the local limit. The value is evaluated at the magnetic axis, rather than over a flux surface, plasma region, or volume, so it is not an average. For an ion species, the population count is summed over all positive ionic charge states and excludes neutral atoms; for electrons, it counts electrons directly. When the population is deuterium–tritium, the mixture is treated as one effective fuel population and includes the ionic charge states of both isotopes. These conventions distinguish particle number density from mass density, charge density, and the density of a single resolved charge state. Species-specific instances include [argon density at the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis), [electron density at the magnetic axis](name:electron_density_at_magnetic_axis), and [deuterium–tritium density at the magnetic axis](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis). The same population-specific density concept at another geometric locus is represented by [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) and [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier); those quantities differ in their evaluation location.

items.name: ion_charge_state_velocity
items.description: Mean bulk-flow velocity vector of ions belonging to one specified ionization charge state, obtained from the first velocity moment of that charge-state population.
items.documentation: The ion charge-state velocity is the mean translational velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state. It describes the charge-state-resolved bulk flow and is distinct from the charge-state-averaged [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity). Let $f_Z(\mathbf{v})$ be the velocity distribution function for ions in charge state $Z$, and let $n_Z$ be their number density. The velocity is defined by $$ \mathbf{u}_Z = \frac{1}{n_Z}\int \mathbf{v}\,f_Z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}, \qquad n_Z = \int f_Z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $\mathbf{u}_Z$ is the charge-state bulk velocity and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity. The vector may be resolved into directional projections, including the [radial ion charge-state velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity), without summing or averaging over other ionization states. Sign convention: Positive components point along the corresponding positive directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

items.name: momentum
items.description: Linear momentum associated with plasma motion, covering concrete quantities that either represent momentum content in a plasma volume or momentum transported through an oriented surface. The specific child name defines whether the quantity is an extensive momentum or a momentum-flux component.
items.documentation: Momentum is the mass-weighted linear-velocity content associated with plasma matter, together with the corresponding transport of that content when the quantity is defined across an oriented surface. As a parent quantity, it denotes the common linear-momentum concept shared by concrete momentum-content and momentum-transport quantities, not a single fully specified observable. This parent must not be interpreted as imposing one governing equation on all children: [plasma momentum](name:plasma_momentum) is an integrated momentum content, whereas [radial momentum](name:radial_momentum) is a component of momentum transport in the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. A concrete child supplies the necessary scope, such as included species, volume integration, component direction, and oriented-surface convention. Sign convention: Positive when a specified component is directed along the positive basis vector or oriented-surface direction named by the concrete child quantity.

items.name: parallel_conductivity
items.description: Local electrical response coefficient relating the electric field along the magnetic field to the conductive current density it drives in plasma.
items.documentation: Parallel conductivity is the local parallel-parallel component of the plasma electrical-conductivity response, with both projections taken along the local magnetic-field direction. It relates the electric-field component along that direction to the conductive current-density component along the same direction. The tensor projection and same-direction conductive response are defined by $$ \sigma_\parallel = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b},\qquad j_\parallel^{\mathrm{cond}} = \sigma_\parallel E_\parallel $$ where $\sigma_\parallel$ is parallel conductivity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the local [plasma electrical conductivity](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity) tensor for the response being described. $E_\parallel$ is the [parallel electric field](name:parallel_electric_field), and $j_\parallel^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive current-density component due to the same-direction parallel response; for the total response, it is the [parallel ohmic current density]. This is a local coefficient for plasma at the location where the response is defined, not a spatial average or integral. For the total plasma response, it represents the combined electrical response of the charged constituents rather than a species-resolved coefficient. When attributed to a particular source, it denotes that source's conductivity contribution and corresponding driven parallel conductive-current response, not the total conductivity. Only the parallel-parallel coefficient is included. Off-diagonal tensor terms, which can also contribute to parallel current when the electric field has transverse components, are distinct from this coefficient; separately driven currents such as bootstrap current are also excluded. Unlike [poloidal conductivity](name:poloidal_conductivity), which selects the poloidal tangent to a magnetic flux surface, or [toroidal conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity), which selects the cylindrical $\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, this projection follows the local magnetic-field direction. Parallel conductivity is a directional component of [plasma electrical conductivity](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity). Its value is governed primarily by electron temperature and Coulomb collisions; for the total bulk-plasma response, it equals Spitzer conductivity in the classical collisional limit.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity
items.description: Parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the field-aligned Fickian diffusivity for thermal-energy transport of a specified ion charge state, defined so the parallel diffusive energy flux is proportional to and opposite the field-aligned gradient of that state's thermal-energy density.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of the thermal-energy density of one specified ionization stage along the magnetic-field direction. It represents the field-aligned Fickian part of that stage's thermal-energy transport, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources, and is the parallel component of ion charge-state energy diffusivity. The defining field-aligned closure is $$ q_{E,z,\parallel} = -\chi_{E,z,\parallel}
abla_\parallel w_z $$ where $q_{E,z,\parallel}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the parallel component of the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ionization stage $z$, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field, $\chi_{E,z,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity, $w_z$ is the thermal-energy density of that ionization stage, and $
abla_\parallel w_z=\mathbf{b}\cdot
abla w_z$ is the field-aligned spatial gradient of that density. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport along the magnetic field. This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over ion species or charge states, unlike [ion energy diffusivity](name:ion_energy_diffusivity). It is a coefficient multiplying the thermal-energy-density gradient, not a temperature-gradient heat-transport coefficient unless the relevant density and heat-capacity factors are explicitly included in the coefficient.

items.name: particle_density
items.description: Particle number density is the concentration of a selected species, including thermal and nonthermal particles and all orbit classes unless a narrower population is specified.
items.documentation: Particle number density is the local concentration of particles belonging to a selected species or population. For the full species distribution, it includes both thermal and nonthermal particles and all orbit classes. The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the distribution function: $$ n_s(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $s$ labels the selected species, $n_s$ is its local particle number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is its particle-number distribution in position and velocity space, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The quantity refers to one selected species, not a sum over different species. For a species specified without charge-state resolution, its number density is summed over all charge states; a charge-state-resolved population retains only the selected state's contribution. The local value does not imply flux-surface averaging; a flux-surface-averaged form averages this same local moment over a magnetic flux surface. The [fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density) is the same moment restricted to suprathermal particles and excludes the thermal population. It contributes to, but is distinct from, the full species density. Distinct nonthermal populations of the same species contribute additively to that full density.

items.name: poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Poloidal flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on poloidal momentum-flux density while preserving the direction or sign assigned to that component by the transport closure.
items.documentation: Poloidal flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on poloidal momentum-flux density in a transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving the sign assigned to the poloidal momentum-flux component by the unconstrained closure. For an unconstrained poloidal momentum-flux density $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}$, a direction-preserving limited flux can be expressed as: $$ \Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}} = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_{\mathrm{pol}} \Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{fs}}\right) $$ where $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited poloidal momentum-flux density, $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure value, $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the non-negative collisionless free-streaming bound for the same poloidal component, and $L_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal flux limiter coefficient. This quantity is the poloidal component of the [momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and a component-specific child of the [flux limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient). It is distinct from the [radial flux limiter coefficient](name:radial_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [toroidal flux limiter coefficient](name:toroidal_flux_limiter_coefficient), and it does not by itself specify a particle species, charge state, neutral internal state, or spatial region. Because $L_{\mathrm{pol}}$ multiplies the non-negative bound $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$, it is a non-negative magnitude-scaling coefficient; the signed direction of the limited flux is carried by $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\Pi_{\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$, not by the coefficient.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Signed poloidal projection of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, along a specified local poloidal direction.
items.documentation: The poloidal component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its signed projection along a specified local poloidal direction. This direction lies in the meridional plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; its positive orientation must be specified. For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is $$ v_{E,\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}. $$ Here $v_{E,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal drift component for the specified ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its ideal E×B drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit vector along the specified positive local poloidal direction. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field and magnetized ions. This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states or species. At fixed local fields, the ideal drift is independent of ion mass and charge. Other contributions to the ion fluid velocity are excluded. It is a linear velocity component, not a poloidal angle or angular velocity. Unlike the [parallel component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), which vanishes identically for the ideal E×B drift, the poloidal projection need not vanish: the local poloidal direction is not generally aligned with the magnetic field. Sign convention: Positive when the E×B drift has a component along the specified positive local poloidal unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying the poloidal temperature gradient of neutral particles in a specified internal state in diffusive thermal-energy transport. It is internal-state-resolved and represents only the Fickian poloidal contribution.
items.documentation:
Fick's-law poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar poloidal diffusivity for energy transport by neutral particles in a specified internal state, and is the poloidal component form of the [neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal states, and relates only the poloidal projection of the diffusive thermal-energy flux to the poloidal temperature gradient of those same particles. The poloidal projection is taken along the tangent obtained by increasing the poloidal angle $	heta$ at constant flux coordinate $ho$ and toroidal angle $\phi$ in a chosen flux-coordinate system $(ho, 	heta, \phi)$. The Fickian poloidal contribution is defined by $$ q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,	heta} = - n_{n,s} D^{	heta}_{E,n,s} \, \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{	heta}\cdot
abla T_{n,s} $$ where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,	heta}$ is the poloidal component of the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, positive in the direction of increasing $	heta$; $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{	heta}$ is the corresponding unit poloidal tangent; $n_{n,s}$ is the number density of those particles; $D^{	heta}_{E,n,s}$ is this coefficient; and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature. The coefficient includes only the diagonal Fickian term driven by $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{	heta}\cdot
abla T_{n,s}$ and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, cross-gradient tensor terms, and effective coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. The factor $n_{n,s}\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{	heta}\cdot
abla T_{n,s}$ is the temperature-gradient contribution to the poloidal gradient of internal thermal-energy density; an energy-density-gradient form using $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{	heta}\cdot
abla(n_{n,s}T_{n,s})$ is equivalent only when the density-gradient contribution along the poloidal tangent is absent. It specializes the internal-state energy diffusion coefficient to neutral particles and the poloidal projection. It is distinct from the [radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [poloidal neutral energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity).

items.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed toroidal angular-momentum transfer density delivered to bulk thermal electrons by collisions with co-passing particles.
items.documentation: This quantity is the toroidal component of the local collisional angular-momentum transfer delivered to the bulk thermal electron population by co-passing particles. It retains only the transfer along the geometric toroidal direction. The toroidal projection is defined by $$ \tau_{\phi,e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}} $$ where $\tau_{\phi,e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the full collisional torque-density vector transferred to thermal electrons from co-passing particles. The unprojected quantity is [co-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Non-toroidal components and transfers involving the counter-passing orbit class are excluded; the latter are represented by [toroidal counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Sign convention: Positive when collisional angular-momentum transfer to thermal electrons points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
items.description: Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and weighted by the first-order Bessel function J1.
items.documentation: Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular kinetic-pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and weighted by the first-order Bessel function. It is the perpendicular projection of the Bessel-1 normalized perturbed pressure moment, associated with particle kinetic energy perpendicular to the background magnetic field. The normalized moment is defined by $$ \hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1} = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2}\, J_1\!\left(k_\perp \rho(v_\perp)\right)\, \delta f_\mathrm{gc}(\mathbf{v})\, d^3v $$ where $\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1}$ is the normalized perpendicular Bessel-1 pressure perturbation, $p_\mathrm{ref}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference thermal pressure, $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference density, $T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference temperature expressed as particle energy, $m$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the background magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function, $k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude, $\rho(v_\perp)$ is the velocity-dependent gyroradius, $\delta f_\mathrm{gc}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity is the perpendicular pressure-tensor projection of [normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1); the complementary field-aligned projection is parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1. It differs from perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure by the first-order Bessel weighting and from perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure by representing the Bessel-1 finite-Larmor-radius contribution rather than the unweighted gyrocenter moment. Sign convention: Positive when, after the eigenmode phase has been fixed by the chosen reference perturbation, the real part of the defining Bessel-weighted perpendicular kinetic-pressure moment represents an excess over the equilibrium gyrocenter distribution.

items.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field
items.description: Complex phasor of the E-plus left-hand circular polarization component of an electromagnetic-wave electric field in a magnetized plasma.
items.documentation: The left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field is the E-plus complex phasor obtained by projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the circular polarization basis transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field. It retains both polarization amplitude and phase and is a component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field). Using the negative-time-harmonic convention, the component is defined by $$ E_{+}=\mathbf{E}_{w}\cdot\mathbf{e}_{+}^{*},\qquad \mathbf{e}_{+}=\frac{\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}+i\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}}{\sqrt{2}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}=\hat{\mathbf{b}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}_{0}}{|\mathbf{B}_{0}|} $$ where $\mathbf{E}_{w}$ is the complex wave-electric-field phasor, $\mathbf{B}_{0}$ is the local background magnetic field, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit direction, the transverse unit vectors $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{1}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{2}$ form a right-handed basis, and the asterisk denotes complex conjugation. The associated physical field uses $\exp(-i\omega t)$, so this component carries phase information rather than representing a field magnitude. Its real-part sibling [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field real part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part) provides one quadrature, while the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field) represents the opposite circular polarization.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude
items.description: Power-deposition-weighted flux-surface amplitude of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus wave-electric-field phasor for each toroidal mode number.
items.documentation: This quantity is the nonnegative amplitude of the right-hand circularly polarized (E-minus, or R-wave) component of a coherent wave electric-field phasor. It represents the mode-resolved field strength after power-deposition-weighted averaging over a magnetic flux surface. For toroidal mode number $n$, the amplitude is defined by $$ \mathcal{E}_{-,n}^{\mathrm{amp}} = \left|\frac{\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\,\widetilde{E}_{-,n}\rangle_{\psi}}{\langle p_{\mathrm{dep}}\rangle_{\psi}}\right| $$ where $\mathcal{E}_{-,n}^{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the amplitude of the E-minus wave-electric-field component, $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $\widetilde{E}_{-,n}$ is its complex phasor, $p_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the power-deposition density, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average, and $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface. The definition applies where the power-deposition-weighted denominator is nonzero. The quantity is restricted to the right-hand circular polarization and to one toroidal mode at a time. It excludes the left-hand circularly polarized component, the total electric-field amplitude obtained by combining polarizations, and an unweighted average or an average of pointwise amplitudes; the modulus is taken after the weighted complex averaging. It is the toroidal-mode-resolved amplitude specialization of the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field amplitude](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude). The corresponding complex E-minus phasor is described by the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), while this quantity retains only its amplitude.

items.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude
items.description: Amplitude representation of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus component of a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor, retaining its polarization direction while removing its complex phase.
items.documentation: The quantity is the amplitude-form representation of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus contribution to a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric field. It retains the polarization basis direction and field strength while excluding the phasor phase. $$ \mathbf{E}_{-,\mathrm{amp}} = |\tilde{E}_{-}|\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{-} $$ Here, $\mathbf{E}_{-,\mathrm{amp}}$ is the amplitude representation of the polarized field component, $\tilde{E}_{-}$ is the complex E-minus coefficient of the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{-}$ is the right-hand circular polarization unit vector transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field. The quantity applies specifically to the right-hand E-minus polarization and excludes the left-hand E-plus component, represented by the [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field). It is an amplitude rather than the full complex phasor and therefore does not retain phase information; it is also distinct from the separate real and imaginary quadratures. The parent quantity imposes no toroidal-mode resolution, flux-surface aggregation, or power-deposition weighting. The [per-toroidal-mode right-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field amplitude](name:per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_amplitude) is a specialization that applies those operations to this common amplitude quantity.
